sense: so I hear, so people say

evidence: Cic. Att. 9.6.2: Domitius, ut audiō, in Cosānō est
Cic. Att. 14.9.2: hīc turba magna est eritque, ut audiō, major
terms.comment: Cicero’s word for news at second hand, set into the sentence; audiō with an accusative and infinitive is “I hear that”.

evidence: Cic. Att. 9.6.2: et quidem, ut ajunt, parātus ad nāvigandum
terms.comment: Of what is going round; it also brings in a proverb, “as the saying goes” (see according to).

terms.gloss: he is said, they are said (to …)
terms.grammar: passive of dīcō, with a nominative and infinitive, or impersonal with an accusative and infinitive
terms.comment: “Apparently he’s left” can be profectus esse dīcitur, “he is said to have left” (Lewis & Short, s.v. dīcō).

phrases.latin: Domitius, ut audiō, in Cosānō est et quidem, ut ajunt, parātus ad nāvigandum
phrases.english: Domitius, apparently, is at his place near Cosa, and ready to sail, they say

phrases.latin: hīc turba magna est eritque, ut audiō, major.
phrases.english: There’s a big crowd here, and apparently it’s going to get bigger.

sources: Lewis & Short: audio · Lewis & Short: aio · Lewis & Short: dico
